text:
William Karlsson has five points in 19 games, and one in his last ten. That looks like a 33-year-old in decline. Our numbers say it's mostly bad luck, and a lot of it.

Vegas has scored 11.3 fewer goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice, one of the biggest gaps in the league. His own shooting is cold too: three goals on 5.0 expected. And the looks keep coming. Last weekend in Buffalo he had a shorthanded breakaway from his own blue line and couldn't get it past the goalie or the rebound into the empty side. That's his season in one sequence.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the slot and taking passes across it, the kind of chances that usually go in. The concern is health and age: he played only 14 games last season, and Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level in that small sample. The original Golden Knight, a Cup winner and a former Lady Byng winner, is due a run. Our range has him around 19 goals by April, which means a lot of them are still coming.
headline: William Karlsson is the unluckiest man in Vegas
